subject: Staged commit schedule & seasonal burst allowance
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@brightlane.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2025-09-10T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Draft: Staged monthly commit proposal for launch

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for the time last week. Per our call I put together a draft monthly commit schedule that tries to account for Brightlane's planned product launch and the expected post-launch tail. The core ideas:

- Start with a modest initial commit in month 1 to limit upfront risk for Brightlane.
- Step-up commits over months 3 and 6 tied to launch milestones (beta -> GA -> scaled ads run).
- A short seasonality/burst allowance for the first 90 days post-GA to absorb launch traffic (with overage pricing at a reduced incremental rate).
- Quarterly true-ups to reconcile usage vs committed units; 30-day notice for changes to commit plan.

Attached is the proposed-commit-schedule.xlsx with numbers baked against the token profile you shared. Pricing notes: we can offer a 15% per-token discount at the Tier 2 commit level (>= 1.2M tokens/mo) and 22% at Tier 3 (>= 3.5M tokens/mo). We're open to structuring the ramp so Brightlane achieves the higher discount once traffic hits the agreed milestones.

Questions for you:
1) Is the 90-day burst window sufficient for the GA aftermath?
2) Would you prefer an absolute token ceiling for burst credits or a %-based buffer?
3) Any procurement constraints on monthly vs quarterly invoicing?

Happy to hop on a 30-min call to walk through the sheet.

Thanks,
Diego
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
attachments: proposed-commit-schedule.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Elena Park <elena.park@brightlane.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2025-09-11T10:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft: Staged monthly commit proposal for launch

Diego —

Appreciate the thoughtful draft. A few points from our side after an internal sync:

- 90 days for burst looks on the short side. Our estimated post-GA spike profile is: 2x baseline for ~30 days immediately after GA, then 1.2–1.5x for the following 60–90 days as paid campaigns and partners ramp. Can you do a 120-day burst window with a sliding taper?
- We prefer a %-based buffer (e.g., +40% of committed tokens in the burst window) rather than an absolute ceiling — gives us flexibility across regions.
- Procurement prefers monthly invoices but needs a clear true-up/true-down process so finance can plan cashflow. Also — any chance the Tier 3 discount can be accelerated if we commit to a 12-month ramp schedule (instead of 6 months)?

Also looping procurement: procurement@brightlane.com for any compliance/redline concerns.

Thanks,
Elena
Head of Growth | Brightlane Inc.

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@brightlane.com>, procurement@brightlane.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2025-09-12T08:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft: Staged monthly commit proposal for launch — updated options

Elena / procurement —

Thanks for the quick feedback. I updated the proposal to reflect two options so Brightlane can pick whichever aligns with risk tolerance:

Option A — Conservative first 3 months, 6-month ramp to Tier 3
- Month 1: 600k tokens
- Month 2: 800k tokens
- Month 3: 1.2M tokens (Tier 2 discount applies)
- Month 4–6: step-up to 3.5M tokens (Tier 3)
- 120-day burst window with +40% buffer (percentage-based)
- Monthly invoices, quarterly true-ups

Option B — Aggressive 12-month ramp to accelerate Tier 3 discount
- Month 1: 400k tokens
- Month 2: 600k tokens
- Months 3–6: linear step to 1.5M tokens
- Months 7–12: reach 3.5M tokens (Tier 3 accelerates if milestones met)
- 120-day burst window with +40% buffer
- If Brightlane signs a 12-month ramp commitment, we can move Tier 3 discount to months 9–12 and offer a one-time 5% launch credit applied to the first two invoices post-GA.

Overage and true-up mechanics: overages during burst are charged at a reduced incremental rate (70% of published per-token list) and reconciled during quarterly true-ups. Unused committed tokens roll forward for up to one quarter.

I've attached an updated PDF (updated-commit-phasing.pdf) that highlights the two options and the cashflow impact. If procurement wants legal/redline language I'll pull counsel in — otherwise happy to take a verbal OK to lock Option A vs B.

Best,
Diego
attachments: updated-commit-phasing.pdf (pdf)

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2025-09-15T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: Approval needed — Brightlane launch credit and burst allowance

Marissa —

We have Brightlane (BL-2025-045) asking for: 120-day burst window (+40% buffer) and a possible one-time 5% launch credit if they sign a 12-month ramp. Pricing asks are within reason but I need approval to commit to the launch credit and to confirm overage at 70% of list.

Option A (6-month ramp) is fine under standard discount bands. Option B (12-month ramp) gives us a shot at more ARR and we can expedite Tier 3 at months 9–12 if milestones are met.

Can you approve a one-time launch credit of 5% applied to the first two invoices post-GA and the 120-day burst window with the % buffer? Legal will still need to sign off on wording around true-ups and roll-forwards.

Thanks,
Diego

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2025-09-16T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: Approval needed — Brightlane launch credit and burst allowance

Diego —

Approve the 5% one-time launch credit for a 12-month ramp commitment. Approve the 120-day burst window with +40% buffer and overage pricing at 70% of list for burst-period overages.

Conditions:
- Add a quarterly business review (QBR) cadence and clear milestone definitions for the months that trigger Tier 3 acceleration.
- Roll-forward of unused committed tokens limited to one quarter only.
- Legal to include a one-month termination notice window in case of sustained non-payment; exclude standard SLA credit language from the launch credit calculation.

Loop in Legal (I've cc'd Ben on this) and go finalize the commercial terms with Brightlane.

-Marissa
VP, Sales | Redwood Inference

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@brightlane.com>, procurement@brightlane.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com, ben_carter@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2025-09-22T15:28:00-07:00
Subject: Final: Staged commit proposal (Option B) + commercial checklist and DocuSign link

Elena / procurement —

Thanks for the collaboration. Per your preference, Brightlane has chosen Option B (12-month ramp). Per Marissa's approval, Redwood will apply:

- A one-time 5% launch credit applied to the first two invoices post-GA.
- A 120-day burst window with a +40% percentage buffer; burst overages charged at 70% of list and reconciled quarterly.
- Quarterly true-ups and monthly invoicing.
- Roll-forward of unused committed tokens limited to the following quarter.
- QBR cadence and defined milestones for Tier 3 acceleration (we'll add milestone language in the SOW).

Next steps:
1) I've uploaded the final commercial sheet and the SOW language to the HubSpot deal (link below).
2) Please review and sign the DocuSign agreement to lock the 12-month ramp and the launch credit: https://docusign.example.com/txn/ABC123DEF
3) Procurement: once signed we'll send an invoice for the first month's commit and schedule the kickoff with our CS team.

HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/brightlane/BL-2025-045
